Regional physical demand was already very strong in places (notably the Far East) and heightened inflationary fears have bolstered that demand. Both gold and silver remain in tight supply, however, and physical premia are high. ##### **Comments from Dr. Bernanke** Possibly one of the more significant influences on market sentiment in recent weeks has come from the Congressional testimony of Federal Reserve Chairman Bernanke, who told the Senate Banking Committee that he thought that higher oil prices would lead, at the most, to a temporary and relatively contained increase in inflation in the United States. He did note, however, that if inflationary expectations were to become heightened then the Fed would be “prepared to respond as necessary to best support the ongoing recovery in the context of price stability”. He also said that accommodative policy has been appropriate, given that there is currently not “really that much of a conflict because inflation and unemployment have been quite low”. Asked whether a combination of high inflation and high unemployment would “create a conflict” for the Fed’s dual mandate over inflation and employment, he said that “I think we’ve learned that [sustained growth is not compatible with] high and variable inflation. So, keeping inflation low and stable is - whatever your mandate - is [sic] absolutely essential and we are committed to doing that”. The Shanghai Gold Exchange did experience a drop in volumes after the New Year holiday, but from a much higher base than in 2010. In our previous One Year Forecast we compared pre-New Year’s Day volumes on the Shanghai Gold Exchange (SGE); this month we are repeating the exercise with post-holiday volumes. In the fortnight following New Year’s Day in 2010, physical (i.e. excluding futures) volumes on the SGE averaged 6.2 tonnes daily, compared with an average of 7.8tpd in the fortnight prior to the holiday; a drop of 21%. This year the daily average after the break was 9.5tpd against 11.7tpd; a drop of 19%, but a year-on-year gain of over 50%. The average daily volume year-to-date in the SGE physical contracts is 10.7 tonnes, a 39% gain yoy. Chin

ese investors remain concerned about local inflationary forces; the latest reported consumer price rise was 4.9% in January and economists are expecting this to ease to 4.7%. Some local observers are of the view that localised inflation is running at considerably higher levels than this. The government continues to raise interest rates and the banks’ reserve requirement ratio in an effort to take the heat out of the system, but the expansion of the local gold market’s infrastructure and the heavy promotion of the metal by a number of banks suggests that there is an underlying momentum in this market that will take some time to slow.
